explanation: Tradition says a priest called it down from the sky around 1700. No one may sit on it, and a British governor's demand to do so in 1900 sparked a war.

claims.text: The Golden Stool is the sacred symbol of the Asante (Ashanti) kingdom, believed to hold the soul of the nation.
The Golden Stool does not belong to Dahomey, Oyo or Songhai.
Asante tradition holds that the priest Okomfo Anokye summoned the Golden Stool from the sky around 1700 for the first king, Osei Tutu.
By custom, no one sits on the Golden Stool.
In 1900 the British governor Frederick Hodgson demanded to sit on the stool, which helped spark the War of the Golden Stool.
